leads.locality: In Koloa along Poipu Road in front of the Kauai Mortuary (Borthwick Kauai Mortuary, a Poipu Road landmark since 1928)
leads.reason: Only one source found (the Hawaii Exceptional Trees register). No independent second source for this specific specimen despite three search attempts; general species-introduction history exists (Earpod planted in Hawaii forest reserves 1926-1935, thousands on Kauai) but that is a class fact, not evidence about this tree, and using it would be a bridge claim. A 2026-05-09 iNaturalist observation of the same species sits ~1.8km away on Poipu Road (outside the register's ~1.1km grid uncertainty), too uncertain to treat as the same tree. Otherwise a strong candidate: large girth (725cm), Excellent vitality, easy Old Koloa Town cluster fit. Worth a second look with a Koloa Heritage Trail plaque check or a direct Street View/site visit confirmation.

leads.locality: On the Grove Farm Homestead grounds among other interesting trees planted by G.N. Wilcox near Highway 501 at Ukukukui

Two search attempts for a second, independent source naming this specific durian tree came back empty; Grove Farm Museum's own well-documented history (buildings, sugar production, irrigation) never mentions a durian. Access would need a paid museum tour (Grove Farm Homestead Museum), which is fine per hard rule 10 as long as access says so, but that is moot without a second source. Worth another look with a call/email to Grove Farm Museum or a Kauai Historical Society search.
